lead_text:
Hello,
We are a family living in Vouliagmeni, with two adults and two children under 18, and we currently have no health insurance policy.
We would like comprehensive coverage for private hospitals, private doctors, specialists, diagnostic tests and emergency visits, including cases where hospital admission is not required.
Our priority is freedom to choose our doctors and private hospitals, with direct payment wherever possible and no requirement to use public hospitals or rely on EOPYY.
Please send us suitable options with low or zero deductibles, the participating hospital list, and details of reimbursement for doctors outside your network. Please also explain any waiting periods, exclusions and annual coverage limits.
Let me know what information you need to prepare a family quotation.
reply_draft:
Hello,

Thank you for your enquiry and for considering Generali as your health insurance provider. Generali is a well-known insurer in Greece, distinguished for its hospital cover and the range of benefits it offers.

You asked about the participating hospital list, direct billing, reimbursement outside the network, waiting periods, exclusions, annual limits and deductibles, and I cover each of these in this reply or in the quotation.

To be fully transparent about your requirements: Generali's programmes cover hospitalisation in Greece very well, but doctors, tests and emergency visits are covered mainly within their partner network. Visits to doctors of your own choice outside the network are limited to a set number a year. In more detail, Generali's flagship plan is Life On, which covers:

* Hospital cover (Hospital Premium Flexi) with an annual capital of €620,000, €940,000 or €1,240,000 per person (the quote I have is €620,000): 100% in Greece and abroad (95% in the USA and Canada) after your participation, and 100% with no participation in public hospitals. [CONFIRM: figures are from a recent quote for one adult]
* Voluntary participation (excess) of €0, €750, €1,500, €3,000, €5,000 or €10,000 a year; a higher participation lowers the premium. With €750 or €1,500, the seven listed serious-illness categories carry no participation.
* Partner hospitals are paid directly by Generali, so you pay only your participation. If another insurer, such as EOPYY, pays more than your participation, a bonus of up to €5,000 a year applies. [CONFIRM: how the bonus applies if you use EOPYY]
* Your choice of room: A (private) or B (semi-private). Room A has a higher premium than the same cover with room B. The quote I have is for room A.
* Wide network of partner hospitals, including Athens: Athens Eye Hospital, Henry Dunant, Euroclinic Athens, Euroclinic Children, ENT Clinic Karras, Iaso, Iaso Children, Iatriko Athinon, Pediatric Center Athens, Iatriko Peristeriou, Iatriko Psychikou, Iatropolis, Leukos Stavros, Metropolitan Hospital, Metropolitan General, Mitera, Mitera Children, Therapis, Hygeia; Thessaloniki: Agios Lucas, Euromedica General Clinic, Euromedica Kyanous Stavros, Iatriko Diavalkaniko Thessaloniki; Other regions: Creta Interclinic (Crete), Iaso Thessalias (Thessaly), Ophthalmica, Laservision.
* Life On is built from modules, so you can add or drop prevention, doctors and exams, hospital, rehabilitation, life cover and accident covers to suit you.
* Doctors & Exams Premium: unlimited visits to partner doctors at €20 per visit, a family doctor at €40 for the first visit and €12 after that, and four visits a year to a doctor of your own choice outside the network, reimbursed up to €20 a visit. Diagnostic tests at partner diagnostic centres up to €2,500 a year with no participation, on a referral from a partner doctor.
* Prevention Standard: an annual check-up (19 tests for adults, 11 for children), with other preventive exams at preferential prices.
* Also in the hospital cover: doctor visits and tests up to 30 days before, and tests, medication and physiotherapy up to 60 days after, the hospital stay; day surgery with no participation; a private nurse for up to 30 days; emergency medical transport up to €5,000 a year in Greece and the EU; a second medical opinion for 13 serious conditions, up to twice per condition; and the option of continuing cover for protected members without a new health check.
* Around the hospital stay: preventive mastectomy or ovary and tube removal up to €5,000 (once) and breast reconstruction up to €5,000 (once); psychological support at €50 a session for up to 10 sessions; legal expenses up to €3,000 a year; emergencies without admission up to €500 per incident, and listed medical procedures up to €1,000 a year, at special partner hospitals with no participation; a newborn allowance of €1,200 in the third insurance year and €1,800 in the fourth.
* If you are hospitalised and do not submit expenses: a daily allowance of €100 (€150 in intensive care) for up to 15 days, and a surgery allowance from €100 to €2,000 depending on the class of operation.

Waiting periods (Hospital Premium Flexi, Article 5): appendectomy the first three months of the first year; nasal growths and tonsillectomy the first year; bowel and genital conditions (except malignancy) and pregnancy complications the first two years; deviated septum, spinal conditions and removal of moles and papillomas the first three years. Doctors & Exams Premium: spinal and knee conditions after the first year. Optional dental cover applies after two years and aesthetic medicine after three. [CONFIRM against the full wording before sending]

Since you are looking for free choice of private doctors and hospitals and outpatient cover for doctors, specialists and tests, we would also like to recommend an international private medical insurance (IPMI) plan as an alternative.

As we have been serving expats and affluent Greeks for many years, working with top-tier international health insurance providers, we have established a strategic collaboration with Generali, so we can guide you to the best insurance solution for your health needs and priorities. Ashlar Assurance is an independent insurance intermediary. We are not employed by Generali and have no employment relationship with it. We are registered with the Athens Chamber of Commerce and Industry in the Special Register of Insurance Intermediaries (registry no. 191526, GEMI 061564903000, in the name of Christos Iatropoulos), and we are responsible for the advice and service we give you. Chris Iatropoulos holds the Chartered Insurance Institute's Award in General Insurance (March 2025). That means we can compare Generali with international providers including VUMI, Bupa, Cigna, Allianz Care, IMG, APRIL International, OneHealth, Now Health and Morgan Price, so you can see both routes. We are paid only by commission from the insurer you choose, and we do not charge you any fee.

IPMI plans can combine:

* Free choice of private hospitals and doctors, with no need for public hospitals or EOPYY
* Outpatient cover for doctors, specialists, diagnostics and prescriptions, with emergency care including visits where admission is not required
* Comprehensive benefits, such as mental health, maternity and complementary therapies

If these are not a high priority, we can instead provide a Generali hospital cover quotation alongside the IPMI one, so you can compare both and decide what suits you best. Generali requires a valid Greek AFM for each adult.

For the Generali option I will send the exclusions and direct billing as the policy wording states them.

For the international options we will also provide the participating hospital list, direct-billing arrangements, reimbursement for out-of-network doctors, waiting periods, exclusions, annual limits and deductible options.

To prepare your quotation, please send us:
1. Dates of birth and nationalities of everyone to be insured
2. Whether each adult holds a valid Greek AFM (Generali requires one)
3. Any existing conditions or ongoing treatment
4. Hospitals or doctors you would like to keep using
5. Whether you want cover in Greece only, Europe, or worldwide
6. Any extras you want, such as maternity, dental, or check-ups
7. Your approximate annual budget
8. Your preferred start date

Best regards,

Chris Iatropoulos
Founder | Ashlar Assurance
M +30 697 590 0189
E c.iatropoulos@ashlarassurance.com
W ashlarassurance.com
Protection built for the life you live.
learned: Generali: hospital cover is strong; emergencies and doctor/specialist visits only within the preferred network, no routine visits to doctors of the client's own choice.
When the lead wants free choice of doctors and outpatient, recommend IPMI with an outpatient module and say the enquiry was passed to the broker.
Offer a Generali hospital-cover quotation alongside the IPMI one for clients who rank outpatient low.
Ask seven questions: dates of birth and nationalities, existing conditions, hospitals/doctors to keep, geographic scope, extras, budget, start date.
Broker's draft did not ask for the Greek AFM or state the commission/no-fee line; the router adds both.
The applicant found a two-route layout unclear; the broker's own draft structure is kept (Generali transparency, IPMI recommendation, Generali hospital quote as the alternative, questions).
Medical Prime figures (visits, tests, physio, hospital partners, waiting periods) come from quote 08547743, issued for one adult; check them against the applicant's own quote.
The applicant did not ask for Medical Prime; the plan name is not mentioned. Name only a plan the lead asked for.
Every request in the lead (hospital list, out-of-network reimbursement, waiting periods, exclusions, limits, deductibles) is acknowledged and either answered or promised for each option.

The algorithm may promise for Generali only what the Generali wordings support (GENERALI_WORDING). Out-of-network reimbursement and prescriptions are stated as not offered and provided only by the international options.

Life On offers a €0 participation option (0, 750, 1,500, 3,000, 5,000, 10,000), so 'low or zero deductible' is no longer a reason to leave Generali; the router now treats it as a review item and the draft states the options.
The broker leads with 'Generali's flagship plan is Life On' when no plan is named, and wants the Life On benefits laid out in full.
The broker softens the IPMI recommendation: 'we would also like to recommend an IPMI plan as an alternative'.

IPMI bullets also list comprehensive benefits (mental health, maternity, complementary). 'No waiting periods' is softened by the router: many plans, apart from maternity, dental, mental and wellbeing.
The EOPYY point is a bonus of up to EUR 5,000 a year when another insurer pays more than the participation; it does not reduce the participation.
The broker's version dropped the bridge, commission disclosure and AFM sentence; the router keeps them until told otherwise.
